how: The initial proposer instantiates the revised starter role without requiring subsequent followers.
Invitations to make the flag instantiate the minimal call for hands without establishing acceptance.
The flag proposals instantiate collective representation at the unanswered proposal end of the range.
A proposed scheme and starting coordinate locate the intended work without establishing an adopted template.
The proposer reconsiders the flag's location relative to another mark before reporting any loss, and a later proposal supplies a separate starting coordinate.
The invitations do not assess hands or space as insufficient.
Asking people to make a flag does not establish a request for an explanation of the canvas or its controls.
The proposals provide no observation of withdrawal under strain or repair of an internal quarrel.
The surviving coded reply revises the proposer's own suggestion rather than accepting a call.
The scheme title proposes making the flag without reporting completed pixels or progress.
The surviving proposals and location revision provide no participant evidence of placement automation.
Proposals and coordinates cannot establish whether actual work proceeded without decided organization.
The scheme title names no chat invitation or report of chat decisions, leaving planning elsewhere unresolved.
The location suggestion and scheme proposal provide no observation of concealing plans or entering rivals' venues.
The calls provide no account of personal time or device constraints on placing.
The scheme title provides no account of site faults or workarounds.
The surviving scheme proposal reports no repair, defence, or conflict between a planned change and the form known to keepers.
The scheme title supplies no attribution of damage or changed pixels.
Reconsidering a proposed location does not report rebuilding after erasure or defeat.
A relative location suggestion does not establish negotiation of a border or agreement.
The alternative locations do not establish restraint toward another mark.
Mentioning another mark as a location reference does not establish exchanged help.
The location revision contains no observed coalition or mutual defence commitment.
Suggesting a position above or on another mark does not establish a host granting space under its rules.
The proposer suggests a location without showing an envoy carrying terms between rooms.
The location suggestion does not establish an argument about the fairness of covering another mark.
Referring to another mark does not establish a member's stated belonging to both rooms.
The location suggestion states neither an authority dispute nor limits on who may commit the room at any stage of making terms.
Proposing a national flag does not establish politics, history, lore beyond the flag, or a colour faith.
The location revision supplies no account of a quarrel inherited from before the canvas.
The location wording establishes neither attack intent nor a prior tie explaining an attack target.
A playful invitation does not establish a new canvas joke taken up by the room.
The flag proposals do not establish formation of a new room around the mark.
The surviving proposals and revision provide no observation of disputes about offence, slurs, or hate symbols.
A smiley invitation does not establish a host April Fools performance or a fake canvas call.
The invitations provide no observation of rules or disputes containing canvas talk.
The calls provide no observation of opposition to canvas posts becoming sabotage of the room's own mark.
The scheme title proposes work rather than celebrating or crediting a completed mark.
A proposed scheme does not record the mark's fate or preserve a reported outcome.
The scheme proposal does not establish a decision to carry the effort beyond the canvas.
The scheme proposal supplies no observation of cleanup disputes, retrospective account correction, or other contests over the preserved event.
The invitations do not establish arrivals attracted by the mark or how members received them.
The proposed scheme does not establish seeking outside creators' or press attention.
Offering positions above or on top of another mark leaves adjacency and overlap open, so attack intent remains unresolved.
The location suggestion does not establish a contest carried through taunts or victory claims.
The proposal and invitation occupy one turn rather than showing a separate starter-to-call sequence.
Calls and a proposed scheme do not establish the building needed to test the call-to-building mechanism.
The surviving coded call receives a self-revision rather than an observed bare join.
The later scheme neither recalls the earlier proposal nor establishes an agreed design, so their order cannot demonstrate design talk settling a template.
Without an established agreement or ensuing limit or refusal, the location suggestion cannot test the bounded agreement-to-authority mechanism.
